summary: Alleghany County, VA fire tower on George Washington NF, destroyed by a forest fire in October 1952; the summit is now reached by an unmarked 1.8-mile hiking trail.

facts.status_note: Destroyed by a forest fire in 1952; no source describes what remains at the summit.

access.note: A trail guide describes an unmarked hiking route with directions from Covington and mentions no closure. No source describes the summit itself.

visit.trail_note: Unmarked 1.8-mile hiking trail from Route 600 that follows an old roadbed and ends at the site of the old tower

events.note: Newspaper item refers to an occupant of the tower on the day of the fire
Forest fire broke out about 15 miles from Covington on Potts Creek road; covered almost 700 acres by the morning of October 28
Item says the fire destroyed the Morning Knob fire tower before crews could check it

notes_for_editor: No source read gives the build date, builder or design of the Morning Knob tower. The 1952 fire is taken from a newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the original newspaper was not checked. The trail guide is undated and its summit remark is not a description of remains. Guessed firetower.org URLs for this site failed (connection reset and 404), so the FFLOS record was not read. Access level 'public' is inferred from the trail guide and no closure is stated there.
